Higgsfield's CEO Alex Mashrabov says the very best engineers and creatives could soon each spend close to $50K to $100K a month on AI.

Harry Stebbings asks him where Higgsfield's internal AI spend, about $4 million or roughly $10,000 per head, will be in 12 months. Alex's guess: it keeps growing for top performers, and he expects those people to ask for comparable salary raises too.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the SF startup hiring humans to walk its robot dogs.

Dimensional, a robotics startup based in San Francisco, is building dimOS, open-source software that lets AI agents control robots using plain-language instructions.

The company posted a job paying $20 an hour for a robot-dog handler: walk alongside a four-legged robot on an outdoor route in downtown San Francisco for four to six hours. No robotics experience needed. The listing has since been taken down.

The point is data. Walkers steer the robots while onboard cameras and sensors record each trip, giving Dimensional real examples of how people navigate city streets so its robots can learn to do it on their own. Founder Stash Pomichter told The New York Times that AI agents are still bad at controlling hardware. One catch from the ad: if a robot overheats, the walker may have to carry it back to the office.

Sources: San Francisco Examiner, Digital Trends.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the YC startup bringing US stock trading to India.

Mochatrade lets traders in India put money in through UPI, in rupees, and trade perpetual futures on US stocks. Perpetuals let a trader bet on a stock going up or down without owning the shares, and they have no expiry date.

Congrats @mochatrade

The company raised a $5.5M seed round led by CoinFund, with Coinbase Ventures and Zero Knowledge Ventures joining. Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund backed it earlier.

Mochatrade was founded in April 2026 by Utkarsh Sinha, Chetan Manda and Parth Maheshwari, and went through the YC Spring 2026 batch. It plans to spend the money on its trading engine and risk systems, and to add contracts tied to pre-IPO companies. Leveraged derivatives are high risk; this is news, not advice.

Sources: The Block, Inc42.

Swipe to see the robotics startup investors want at $20B.

Physical Intelligence builds AI models meant to work as a general-purpose brain for robots, so the same model can control many kinds of machines.

Bloomberg reports the company is in early talks to raise at least $1B at a valuation of about $20B, with existing backers Avenir and Lux Capital reportedly leading. Nothing is final and terms could change.

That would nearly double the roughly $11.5B valuation it reportedly reached earlier this year, and the company is still pre-revenue. Founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers and academics from Stanford and UC Berkeley, it opened beta access to its latest robot models for outside developers earlier this month.

Sources: Bloomberg, Quartz.
